If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in late horizon (days 25–30) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid horizon (days 15–24) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast downward by 2–3% in the 3–5 day window following the reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.33) across 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias in early horizon (days 1–10) to compensate for low confidence.  
If sentiment peaks at day 1–3 and then declines, reduce forecast by 1–2% in days 4–7 to reflect sentiment decay.  
If sentiment is high at day 1–2 but drops to low by day 5, increase forecast by 1–2% in days 8–10 to offset sentiment-induced volatility.
